Home
Headteacher's Welcome
At Hindhayes, we believe success is based on the partnerships between pupils, staff and the parent community. We endeavour to enrich and develop each child to be a successful individual that will become an active community citizen of the future.
Download our Newsletter
What's New at Hindhayes Infant School
Children are invited to support Children In need this Friday the 13th November by wearing something spotty with their home clothes. Please ensure clothes are warm for outside and flexible for those children who have PE. A suggested donation of £2 to be shared between supporting children in our school and children nationally.
Join our friendly team at Hindhayes Infant School! Are you someone who takes pride in their work, has a good eye for detail and understands the importance of maintaining high standards of cleanliness? Hindhayes Infant School is looking to appoint a reliable, hardworking and conscientious Cleaner to join our team. We are a friendly infant school providing education for children aged 4–7 years old. Maintaining a clean, safe and hygienic environment is particularly important in our school, helping to ensure that our children can learn, play and thrive in surroundings that are welcoming, healthy and well cared for. We are therefore looking for the right person who takes pride in their work, has high standards and is committed to ensuring that these standards are consistently maintained throughout the school. The Position Hours: 15 hours per week Working pattern: Monday to Friday Working times: 3.00pm - 6.00pm Contract: Term time plus 3 additional weeks for deep cleaning Salary: Grade 17 – £13.2764 per hour The Person We are looking for someone who: Takes pride in their work and has excellent attention to detail. Is reliable, conscientious and hardworking. Understands the importance of high cleaning and hygiene standards, particularly in an environment used by young children. Can work independently and manage their time effectively. Is a positive team player who takes a real sense of responsibility for their role within our school. This is an important role within our school community, and the successful applicant will play a key part in ensuring that our children and staff enjoy a clean, safe and welcoming environment every day. Interested? If you think you could be the right person for our team and would like to find out more, please contact Mike Sales, Business Manager, who will be happy to provide further information, an application form together with a copy of the Job Description and Person Specification. Email - Mike.Sales@Hindhayes.co.uk call (01458) 444931 or pop into the school office.
Vacancy! We are looking to appoint a friendly and energetic Midday Supervisor Assistant (MDSA) to join our Hindhayes team. The role involves supporting and supervising children during their food and lunchtime, both indoors and outdoors. Hours: 11:45am – 1:00pm, Monday to Friday (6.25 hours per week, term time only) Pay: Grade 16, £13.27 per hour Closing Date: 20 November 2026 Interview Date: To be confirmed For further information and an application form, please contact Mike Sales - Mike.Sales@Hindhayes.co.uk
School Photos! In a couple weeks, we shall be taking individual school photos. These will be taken with a plain backdrop as well as a Christmas style backdrop, making the perfect Christmas gifts for the family! After great success last year, we will again be offering family portraits too. These are bookable via Scott in the Office, and slots will be available after school.
Please come and enjoy our Autumn Fayre tomorrow at 3.00pm. Thank you so much for your support of this event already. We just need some yummy cakes to sell alongside our drinks and hot food offer. Fingers crossed for the sun!
On Thursday, we shall be holding our Autumn Fayre from 3pm to 5pm. Food and Drink We will be selling hot drinks on site. There will be hot dogs, burgers, veggie burgers and soup available from the kitchen at £1.50. We kindly ask that you pre order where possible for this, however payment will be taken from the kitchen on the day. Tokens This year we will be introducing the idea of pre purchased tokens. These are available to be purchased on ParentMail at either £5 or £10. This will enable to you be pre paid for all activities. Activities will cost £1 on all stalls. You will still be able to pay cash or card on the day. Cake Donations If any of our fabulous parents would like to bake some cakes to donate for us to sell at the fayre, we kindly ask these come in on Thursday. In line with school policy, we ask that you avoid the use of any nut products. Thank you.
This week we will be collecting Harvest donations in the entrance hall to support the work of the Salvation Army in our community. Please help to come together to ensure all our families have enough to eat. See photograph for donations needed. Thank you in advance for your support of our community.
We are looking for some help to create something like this in our recycling area at the rear entrance to the school. Is there anyone who could offer to help build it or suggest someone who could. If you do please email Mike (Mike.Sales@Hindhayes.co.uk), call on 444931 or pop into the office. Thank you

Headteacher's Welcome
Once again, welcome to Hindhayes Infant School.
At Hindhayes, we believe success is based on the partnerships between pupils, staff and the parent community. We endeavour to enrich and develop each child to be a successful individual that will become an active community citizen of the future.
At Hindhayes we have the highest of expectations of all our members of the school. Through high quality teaching, an engaging curriculum and excellent pastoral care we want all of our pupils to develop the skills and knowledge that they need to be ready for the next stage of their learning journey. With this in mind we work very closely with Elmhurst Junior school, our main feeder school for pupils leaving us at the end of Year 2.
Our website has been designed to give you a flavour of the learning experience that we offer to very young children, however there it is no substitute for visiting our school and so we urge you to come and visit us when the children are working so that you can see first-hand the caring environment that our staff work so hard to establish. Please contact the school office and I will be very happy to take the time to show you and your child around our beautiful school.
Mrs Kate Nester Headteacher

School Vision
Please click on the link below to open the document.
School Vision»

Values
At Hindhayes we strive to inspire and develop positive values within our pupils.
Values are the things that we believe in (our beliefs) and strive for (our ideals). They guide our actions, our thinking and how we feel about ourselves. They make us who we are.
Within education a strong commitment to a structure for the promotion of strong values can; develop a positive ethos and increase self-esteem, improve standards of behaviour and so raise academic achievement.
Values are promoted through; a structured two year programme, a half termly whole school focus, whole school assemblies, classroom circle time session, whole school and classroom rules, displays, whole school ethos, the support and work of the learning mentor, positive role models, school newsletters, support from parents and carers.
The work done in this area is underpinned by the British Values; Democracy, Individual Liberty, The Rule of Law, Mutual Respect, Tolerance of Those who have different faiths and beliefs.

Parents
Whether you are a current parent of a child at Hindhayes or looking for a new school for your child, you should be able to find out all you need to know here.
Mission Statement
We believe that learning is a lifelong activity which engages everyone in our school community. We see every activity as a learning opportunity and nurture a love of learning through building self esteem and enthusiasm. We endeavour to create a happy, purposeful environment where everyone feels valued and able to reach their full potential.
If you still have any questions please call the school office, we will be pleased to help you. Paper copies of the information included in this website are available from the school office on request.

Use the tabs on the left to explore the curriculum Hindhayes School has developed.
Core Subjects are: English, Maths, Science
Foundation Subjects are: Computing, History, Geography, Art, Design and Technology, Music and Physical Education.
Statutory Subjects are: Religious Education, Health Education and Relationship Education Hindhayes has chosen to combine Relationship Education with Personal, Health and Social Education as well as aspects of teaching Citizenship, which we call Curriculum For Life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hindhayes Infant School - English as an Additional Language
pageCache.text:
English as an Additional Language
Intent – EAL at Hindhayes
Recent research to inform practice: In September 2019, the ‘School Inspection Handbook’ was released by Ofsted with a clear shift of focus on language and vocabulary acquisition for all pupils. This was further supported by the previously released Ofsted guidance video entitled ‘Vocabulary and Reading’ in December 2018. In the handbook it mentions that schools have a ‘sharp focus on ensuring that younger children gain phonics knowledge and language comprehension necessary to read, and the skills to communicate’. Alongside this Ofsted are looking for a ‘sharp focus on ensuring that children acquire a wide vocabulary’. Ofsted emphasise the importance of teachers modelling their own good use of language and vocabulary, ensuring they are reading to children, introducing new concepts with new vocabulary. They mention the idea that early years children need to develop vocabulary to use across the curriculum and how this is successfully achieved through stories, poems, rhymes, and non-fiction being regularly read to children. In the Ofsted video ‘Vocabulary and Reading’ Ofsted advise that educational programmes are set-up to focus on increasing children’s vocabulary, their understanding of words and their ability to use words in different contexts. They state the best way of developing vocabulary is by having a broad and rich curriculum and that it is essential that teachers know what vocabulary is going to be taught within this. Proven research states that the wider the vocabulary of a pupil, the more academic success they will achieve.
Developing EAL learners at Hindhayes: We aim to settle the children into school life as soon as possible and to encourage them to take part in daily routines and structures which will help them to develop an understanding of the academic aspects of English as well as the use of our language as a social interaction. We work with parents/careers to ensure a smooth transition into school, to carry out an entry interview to find out details about the child’s past school experiences, their preferred methods of learning, their previous exposure to English, and any traumatic experiences the children might have had. We celebrate the fact that a rising number of children attending Hindhayes school speak more than one language and take account of each child’s life experiences and needs when planning our curriculum. We acknowledge that children who are learning English as an additional language have skills and knowledge about language similar to monolingual English-speaking children and that their ability to participate in the full curriculum may be in advance to their communicative skills in English.

Hindhayes History
Hindhayes School has a rich heritage. The School was founded by Roger and Sarah Clark and the links with the Clark Foundation are still strong today.
Its character and ethos remain based on Christian traditions and principles. The School enjoys strong and well founded links with the community and is a long established source of pride within the town. It’s building is centred around an attractive quadrangle which stands in extensive grounds dating from 1928. The classrooms are light and airy with stimulating displays to support the children’s learning and achievement.

This strategy addresses the schools' individual context, the barriers for learning identified through triangulation of evidence and the planned activities to diminish these differences through improved inclusion.
